items.title: 68189_Al Hall oral history interview
items.q: I knew Sonny Rollins when he was a baby.

ctx.x: In what period are you referring now?

'40, late '40s, '50s. All a guy had to do was have a tenor saxophone during that period, and he recorded. And it wasn't necessarily professional up to the point of Coleman Hawkins or Lester Young. I knew Sonny Rollins when he was a baby. He was put out too fast, and he suffered for it for a length of time, his loneliness and of trying to get himself together, because he was pushed. Then, well, there's mostly for (inaudible) tenor saxophone players, anyhow. Tenors prevailed over altos, trumpet players, and whatnot…
What do you think about Mingus' contributions?
